items.title: The fibre-dimension bound and the semismallness of the projective morphism between two quiver varieties
items.author: Hiraku Nakajima
items.source_version: Official SIGMA 5 (2009) article 003, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2009.003; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-10-01, exact bytes pinned by SHA256
items.difficulty_reason: The counted statement is the pair of results that make the morphism between the two quiver varieties well behaved (author Proposition at source lines 1553-1575, label prop:semismall): the fibre over a point of a stratum has dimension at most half the difference of the dimensions of source and stratum, and the map restricted to its image is semismall for the stratification by the images of the strata. Part (1) is a strengthening of a result proved in the cited paper under the extra hypothesis that the regular part of the target moduli space is non-empty, and the content is the author's observation that the original proof works without it, the mechanism being that the fibre of the lifted map over the origin sits inside an affine algebraic manifold with the trivial factor removed (proof lines 1578-1586). Part (2) then combines the fibre-bundle property of the restrictions with the dimension bookkeeping forced by part (1) (proof lines 1588-1593). H2.
